verdicts.title: AGENTS.md's "Accounting native module" section is factually wrong on all three of its claims and contradicts AGENTS.md's own package table
verdicts.reasoning: Verified all three statements independently in the current tree. AGENTS.md:191-200 (the '### Accounting native module' block) says the compiled artifact is `opaque/accounting/opaque_accounting.abi3.so`, that maturin uses `module-name = "opaque.accounting.opaque_accounting"` with `python-packages = ["opaque.accounting"]`, and that `opaque.accounting/__init__.py` does `from . import opaque_accounting as _native`. None holds: packages/opaque-accounting/pyproject.toml:38-40 sets `module-name = "opaque.api.accounting.core.opaque_accounting"` and `python-packages = ["opaque/accounting", "opaque/api/accounting/core"]`; the only built .so in the tree is packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/opaque_accounting.abi3.so (and the importable `_native.__file__` resolves there); `grep -rn 'as _native' packages/opaque-accounting/src/` matches exactly one line, packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/__init__.py:16, and the `opaque.accounting` facade __init__.py contains no such import. The same file's package table (AGENTS.md:32) already states the extension is at `opaque.api.accounting.core.opaque_accounting` aliased as `_native`, so AGENTS.md contradicts itself, and .github/scripts/check_accounting_artifact_policy.py:23 pins NATIVE_MODULE_PATH = "opaque/api/accounting/core/opaque_accounting.abi3.so", i.e. CI agrees with the code. Severity stays low: this is agent-facing documentation drift with no runtime, build or privacy effect - the build itself is driven by pyproject.toml, not by AGENTS.md, and the correct path is stated twice elsewhere (table row + CI script), so an agent has ready contradicting evidence. Not a duplicate of open Bazalt #775/#845, whose open child scope is citation verification, not the native-module layout note.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: AGENTS.md:191-200 states three facts about the PyO3 extension layout that are all false at HEAD (artifact path, maturin module-name/python-packages, and where the `_native` alias is bound), and contradicts AGENTS.md:32 in the same file. An agent that trusts this section looks for `opaque/accounting/opaque_accounting` - which does not exist - or proposes reverting the maturin configuration to a layout the wheel-policy check (.github/scripts/check_accounting_artifact_policy.py) would reject. No runtime, build or privacy impact; the cost is wasted agent/reviewer time, mitigated by the correct path appearing in the same file's package table and in the CI script.

verdicts.title: Gemma2 silently loses its sliding window under SDPA when attn_logit_softcapping is None
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced independently at two levels with transformers 5.15.1 / torch 2.14.0. (1) Code path: models/gemma2.py:30-36 pairs `sdpa_attention_replacement=vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2` with `masking_module_patcher=apply_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_masking_patch`; that patcher (components/masking.py) installs `vmap_create_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_causal_mask`, which returns None (no mask) when `_can_use_compact_sdpa_sliding_window` holds (runtime/masking.py:78-107: sdpa, attention_mask is None, no cache, cache_position None, no or/and mask fns, dropout 0 or no grad, seq_len > sliding_window) - and that predicate never consults `attn_logit_softcapping`. `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2` (components/attention.py:670-738) honours `sliding_window` only inside the `softcap is not None` branch; the final `return vmap_sdpa_attention_forward(module, q, k, v, attention_mask, dropout=..., scaling=..., **kwargs)` drops `sliding_window`, which is a named parameter of the enclosing function and therefore not in **kwargs, and `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward` (attention.py:169-240) has no window handling. (2) My own unit test (H=4 q-heads, S=16, D=8, window 4, float64, both kvh=2 GQA and kvh=1): `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2(..., softcap=None, sliding_window=4)` matches a plain full-causal reference to 8.9e-16 and deviates 2.83 from the explicit windowed reference, while `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_sliding_window` matches the windowed reference to 4.4e-16. (3) My own end-to-end test: Gemma2Config(hidden_size=32, 4 layers -> layer_types ['sliding_attention','full_attention',...], 4 heads / 2 kv, head_dim 8, sliding_window=4, attention_dropout=0.0), _attn_implementation='sdpa', float64, input_ids shape (1,24), unpatched vs apply_runtime_patches()+apply_model_patches(model): max|logit diff| = 0.1065 with attn_logit_softcapping=None versus 6.6e-08 with the default 50.0 (mean |logit| 0.081). Passing an all-ones attention_mask on the same softcapping=None model gives exactly 0.0 diff, isolating the mask-is-None compact path as the cause. Coverage gap confirmed: `_SLIDING_WINDOW_FAMILIES = {"ministral", "mistral"}` in tests/transformers/models/test_parity.py:57 excludes gemma2, and test_parity.py:348 pins `attn_logit_softcapping = 50.0`, so the None branch with no mask is untested. Delta provenance confirmed: `git log -S` shows d80d3f99 (#954) added the masking patcher to gemma2; before it the dense mask always carried the window. Severity lowered from high to medium: the defect needs attn_logit_softcapping explicitly set to None (every released Gemma2 checkpoint ships 50.0), sdpa, seq_len > sliding_window (4096 on real checkpoints), and attention_mask omitted entirely - and opaque's own trainers always pass attention_mask (_dp_trainer.py, trl/_sft_trainer.py:586,610, trl/_dpo_trainer.py:1113,1118), which forces the dense correct path. It is still silent (no error or warning) and wrong-numerics, so not low. No epsilon impact.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: With opaque's gemma2 patches applied, a Gemma2 model configured with `attn_logit_softcapping=None`, `_attn_implementation='sdpa'`, `attention_dropout=0.0`, a sequence longer than `sliding_window`, and called WITHOUT an `attention_mask`, runs its sliding layers as full causal attention: the compact masking patcher returns None and `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2`'s softcap-None fall-through drops `sliding_window`. Measured on a tiny float64 Gemma2 (4 layers, sliding_window=4, seq_len=24): patched-vs-unpatched logits differ by 0.1065 max-abs against a mean |logit| of 0.081, versus 6.6e-08 with the default softcapping of 50.0 and exactly 0.0 when an all-ones attention_mask is supplied. Unit-level, the softcap-None path matches full-causal SDPA to 8.9e-16 and deviates 2.83 from the windowed reference. Silent - no error or warning. Not reachable through opaque's own DPTrainer / SFT / DPO paths, which always pass attention_mask, and not reachable with any released Gemma2 checkpoint's default softcapping; it needs the explicit softcapping=None configuration plus direct model(input_ids=...) calls. No effect on epsilon.

verdicts.title: New random-allocation lru_cache retains native PLD handles past calibrate's cache teardown, with a docstring that denies it
verdicts.reasoning: Verified every link with the prebuilt extension (packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/opaque_accounting.abi3.so). _random_allocation_cache.py wraps `_native.random_allocation_gaussian_pld` in `@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=8)`; its return type is `Pld`, and _base.py:60 is `Pld: TypeAlias = _native.Pld`, i.e. a PyO3 Rust-backed object - so the module docstring's 'bounded LRU over immutable Python Pld objects (no native handles), so it is self-limiting and needs no byte budget or destructor' is wrong on 'no native handles'. The cache is a bare functools LRU and never joins `_native_cache._registry` (the only `NativeCache(` construction outside tests is the factory at _native_cache.py:186, used by the dpftrl b-min-sep transcript cache), so `_clear_all_native_caches()` (calibration.py:357, in `finally`) cannot touch it; only `clear_random_allocation_caches()` / `epoch_pld.cache_clear()` empties it. Measured: `cal.calibrate(cal.epsilon_budget(3.0, delta=1e-5), lambda nm: k_out_of_t(gaussian(nm), k=4, t=64, allocation='block'), 0.5, 4.0)` ends with `CacheInfo(hits=0, misses=22, maxsize=8, currsize=8)` and `_clear_all_native_caches()` leaves currsize at 8 (explicit cache_clear drops it to 0) - so the cache yields zero hits during calibration (each probe has a distinct noise multiplier) and purely retains. Memory: 8 distinct `epoch_pld(sigma_i, 64, 4, default_config)` handles took RSS 18.1 -> 189.1 MB, and `cache_clear()` returned 78.8 MB; a warm-allocator run gave 97.0 MB for 4 entries with 76.2 MB returned on clear, i.e. roughly 10-20 MB retained per entry, not the documented '~0.5 MB per entry'. The 0.5 MB figure corresponds to 2 x max_conv_grid(32768) x 8 B, but the retained PLD grid is bounded by max_grid_size, which defaults to 10,000,000. Severity stays low: the cache is bounded at 8 entries (no unbounded leak), nothing here affects epsilon or numerical results, and `calibrate`'s own docstring is narrowly worded ('Native LRU caches registered via ... _native_cache') so only the module docstring is untrue. Not a duplicate of open #911 (Monte Carlo calibration performance).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A process that calls `calibrate` over a k-out-of-t or balls-in-bins process leaves up to 8 Rust-backed PLD objects alive in the unregistered `epoch_pld` lru_cache after the search finishes: measured `CacheInfo(hits=0, misses=22, currsize=8)` after one calibrate, unchanged by `_clear_all_native_caches()` in calibrate's `finally`. Retained memory is roughly 10-20 MB per entry (78.8 MB returned to the OS when the 8-entry cache is cleared explicitly; 76.2 MB for 4 entries in a warm-allocator run), against a module docstring that claims '~0.5 MB per entry' and 'no native handles ... needs no byte budget or destructor'. Bounded at 8 entries, so this is a fixed ~100-200 MB resident footprint in a long-lived accounting service plus an incorrect docstring, not an unbounded leak; no effect on epsilon or on any computed number, and the cache returns zero hits during calibration so the retention buys nothing there.

verdicts.title: Python 3.12 is still advertised by every wheel and executed by no CI lane
verdicts.reasoning: Verified directly: `grep -rn '3\.12' .github/workflows/` returns nothing, while every explicit interpreter pin is 3.11 or 3.13 (ci.yml:56,69,117,131; pr.yml:96,109,165,182; build-distributions.yml:37,129; prepare-release-implementation.yml:335,353,421,440; validate-distributions.yml:19 matrixes exactly ["3.11", "3.13"]). The reusable python-tests.yml defaults `python-version` to "3.11" (line 37) and every caller in ci.yml / pr.yml either passes 3.11/3.13 or takes that default; the composite .github/actions/setup-python also defaults to "3.11". Meanwhile pyproject.toml:12 declares `requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.14"` and pyproject.toml:29 the `Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12` classifier, repeated per package (e.g. packages/opaque-accounting/pyproject.toml:24), so pip installs the abi3 wheels on 3.12 with no CI signal behind them. Severity stays low and I would not raise it: testing the supported endpoints and relying on abi3 for the native wheel is a defensible, common policy, nothing here is a defect that produces wrong output, and no privacy guarantee is touched - the finding is a coverage/metadata consistency gap. Referenced trackers (Slate #428, Bazalt #841 / OPQ-386) are not in the open-issue lists, so this is not an open duplicate; note it does re-open ground covered by a closed issue rather than being a fresh defect.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: No workflow in .github/workflows runs Python 3.12 (no occurrence of the string anywhere; validate-distributions matrixes only 3.11 and 3.13, python-tests.yml and the setup-python composite both default to 3.11), yet every distribution declares `requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.14"` plus the 3.12 classifier, so pip resolves and installs on 3.12. A 3.12-only regression - a dependency resolving differently, or interpreter-specific behaviour in the torch.func / optree layer - would ship unnoticed and be first seen by users. Bounded: 3.11 and 3.13 bracket most interpreter-sensitive behaviour, the native extension is a single cp311-abi3 wheel shared across all three, and no privacy guarantee or computed result is affected. This is a CI-coverage / metadata-consistency gap, not a defect in the library.
